title: KV-cache-aware tokens/sec microbench and regression detector
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark suite that explicitly accounts for KV-cache warm vs cold states, multiple batch sizes, sequence-length distributions, and quantization variants. This harness will be the canonical perf signal for QA/CI for core models used in hosted and dedicated deployments.

Scope:
- Microbench harness that runs synthetic and recorded prompt traces against model containers across GPU families (A100/H100) and quantization modes (fp16, int8).
- Test vectors: seq lengths [8, 32, 128, 512], batch sizes [1,4,8,16], KV-cache cold vs warmed (0, 1, 8 requests in cache), and short/long context synthetic mixes.
- Metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-second sliding), p50/p90/p95 latency for token generation, tail variance, and error rates (OOMs, timeouts).
- Statistical regression detection: rolling baseline (14d), bootstrap CIs, non-parametric tests for latency distribution changes (Mann-Whitney U) and relative throughput drop detection.
- CI integration: Buildkite job 'perf/microbench' triggered nightly and on PRs tagged with 'perf-affecting'. Fail CI if TPS drops >7% with p<0.01 against baseline or if p95 increases by >20ms.
- Observability: push results to Grafana dashboard and S3 artifact store; attach run artifacts and sample traces to PRs automatically.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Harness can run a full matrix (all seq lengths x batch sizes x kv-states x quant modes) in <3 hours for a single model on dedicated infra and produce a single consolidated JSON report.
2) Regression detector is configured with configurable thresholds and produces Slack alerts with links to diffs and raw artifacts.
3) CI gating job added and documented; example PR demonstrates a perf regression alert and triage flow.
4) Daily summary report (email/Slack) with rolling 14-day baseline and detected anomalies.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Synthetic vs recorded traffic: synthetic traces are deterministic and cheap; recorded traces capture real distribution. We'll run both but prioritize recorded traces for baseline.
- Statistical test choice: Mann-Whitney useful for non-normal latency distributions; we also add bootstrap of TPS ratio to get CI on percent change.
- Running full matrix is expensive; initial CI gating will run a lightweight smoke matrix (seq 32 & 128, batches 1 & 8, warm/cold) and the nightly full matrix.
- KV-cache semantics: "warmed" defined as pre-populating KV with 8 repeating continuation tokens to approximate long-running sessions. We will add a config knob for more realistic warmup per customer profile later.

Artifacts & links: perf spec doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/perf/microbench/kv-cache-spec-2025; example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124; dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Perf/TPS-microbench; sample run artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/microbench/2025-02-27/ENG-11024-run-001.zip

Longer term: integrate RL-based anomaly detector for early signal, extend to multi-tenant noise experiments, and add support for on-prem kits in 'private' mode to ensure parity across deployment modes.
